source: Dış kaynaklarda saptanan eksik soru tipleri; bağımsız anlatım ve resmî cevap kontrolü (2026-10-12)
answer_convention: İki dilde aynı sırada; ilk şık doğru. Belirsiz cevap aktif bankada yok.
id_convention: Kalıcı idler_010.json; eski veya emekli kimlik yeniden kullanılmaz.

questions.text: Which aeroplane reference field length corresponds to aerodrome reference code number 3?
options: At least 1,200 m but less than 1,800 m
At least 800 m but less than 1,200 m
More than 1,200 m up to and including 1,800 m

questions.text: Which aerodrome ATS units determine the transition level from the QNH reports?
options: Approach Control Office or the Aerodrome Control Tower

questions.text: What makes an aerodrome a controlled aerodrome?
options: An air traffic control service is provided to its aerodrome traffic
It must always lie inside a control zone
It has more than one runway

questions.text: For the aerodrome reference code, what reference field length corresponds to code number 4?
How many light units normally make up one PAPI wing bar?
Under Part-FCL, what is the minimum age for issue of a commercial pilot licence?
What does the number in an aerodrome reference code describe?
options: Aeroplane reference field length for planning
The actual runway length in every case

questions.text: Between FL290 and FL410 in designated RVSM airspace, what nominal vertical separation is applied to appropriately approved aircraft?
For a departing aircraft that has not already received the setting, when should QNH be included in the ATC clearance sequence?
options: Only if an IFR pilot asks

questions.text: Under Part-MED, what class of medical certificate is required to exercise CPL privileges?
What defines a special VFR flight under SERA?
options: A VFR flight cleared by ATC to operate inside a control zone in conditions below VMC
Any VFR flight outside controlled airspace
A flight with no radio and no clearance

questions.text: Which temporary AIP change normally requires an AIP Supplement rather than a short ordinary notice?
options: A change lasting three months or longer, or a shorter change needing extensive text/graphics
Only a change lasting more than one year

questions.text: On the normal PAPI approach slope, what does the pilot see?
options: Two red and two white units
One red and three white units

questions.text: What is the normal IFR vertical separation minimum in controlled airspace below FL290?
Under Part-MED, from what date is the validity of an initial medical certificate normally calculated?
options: The date of the aeromedical examination
The date the pilot licence is printed
The date the aircraft is registered
The first flight after the examination

questions.text: An IFR pilot elects to continue as VFR in suitable airspace and expects uninterrupted VMC. What must the pilot do?
options: Notify ATS explicitly that IFR is cancelled and communicate flight-plan changes
Wait for automatic cancellation on reaching VMC
Cancel only when instructed by ATC
Keep the change secret until landing

questions.text: For Chicago Convention sovereignty, what does a State’s territory include?
options: Its land areas and adjacent territorial waters
Every FIR it provides services in

questions.text: Which rules govern flights over the high seas under SERA?
options: ICAO Annex 2 Rules of the Air without exception
Only the nearest State’s domestic rules

questions.text: Besides a valid pilot licence, what documents must a Part-FCL pilot carry while exercising its privileges?
options: A valid medical certificate and a personal photographic ID
A passport instead of the medical

questions.text: You overtake another aeroplane from behind while climbing. Does the climb remove your obligation to give way?
options: No; pass to its right and remain clear until entirely past and clear
Yes, because the climb creates priority
Only if the other aeroplane is also climbing

questions.text: Flashing anti-collision lights in cloud interfere with the pilot’s safe performance of duties. May the pilot reduce or switch them off?
options: No, even if duties are impaired

questions.text: An IFR aircraft flies outside controlled airspace along a route designated for flight-plan and FIS communication requirements. What radio duty applies?
options: Maintain a listening watch and establish two-way communication as necessary
No radio duty applies outside controlled airspace
Change to VFR to contact FIS

questions.text: Which ICAO body considers and recommends technical Annex amendments to the Council?
options: The aircraft State of registry alone

questions.text: Under ordinary SERA rules, what is the speed limit for an aeroplane VFR in Class E below 10,000 ft AMSL, unless a permitted exception applies?
What does emergency phase mean in ATS terminology?
options: A generic term for uncertainty, alert or distress phase, as applicable

questions.text: A normal VFR flight operates in Class E outside any radio mandatory zone. Which statement is correct?
options: No ATC clearance or continuous two-way radio is required by the class alone, and ATC separation is not provided to VFR
ATC separates it from every IFR flight
An ATC clearance is always required
Two-way radio is always mandatory for all VFR

questions.text: An IFR flight is cleared for a visual approach in Class C. From which traffic is it normally separated by ATC?
options: No traffic after accepting the visual approach

questions.text: For a VFR flight plan, what does total estimated elapsed time measure?
options: From take-off to arrival over the destination aerodrome
From entering controlled airspace to landing

questions.text: Which aircraft is a strayed aircraft?
options: One significantly off its intended track, or one reporting that it is lost
Only an aircraft without a flight plan

questions.text: How may a pilot legally fly in a published restricted area?
options: In accordance with the published restrictions or with the relevant State’s permission
Only by filing an IFR flight plan
Whenever the aircraft is below cloud

questions.text: For VFR in Class G above the higher of 3,000 ft AMSL or 1,000 ft above terrain, but below 10,000 ft AMSL, what vertical cloud clearance is normally required?
At an uncontrolled aerodrome, what is the normal circuit-turn direction if no different pattern is indicated?
For VFR in Class G above the higher of 3,000 ft AMSL or 1,000 ft above terrain, but below 10,000 ft AMSL, what is the normal horizontal cloud clearance?
options: Clear of cloud with no fixed distance

questions.text: Under ordinary SERA special VFR rules for an aeroplane by day, what minimum flight visibility must the pilot maintain?
options: 1,500 m, clear of cloud with the surface in sight

questions.text: While passing through the transition layer, how is an aircraft’s vertical position normally expressed during climb and during descent?
options: Flight levels during climb; altitudes during descent
Altitudes during both climb and descent
Flight levels during both climb and descent
Altitudes during climb; flight levels during descent

questions.text: Unless a competent authority or ATC specifies otherwise, above what height does day VFR level cruising normally follow the cruising-level table?
options: 3,000 ft above mean sea level everywhere

questions.text: A VFR aeroplane cruises above the table threshold on true track 170° with variation 20°W. Which listed standard cruising level fits its magnetic track?
Which quantity determines the ordinary east/west VFR cruising-level band?
options: Magnetic track, with odd thousands plus 500 ft for 000°–179°
True heading, with odd thousands plus 500 ft for 000°–179°

questions.text: An airship and a balloon converge at the same level. Which must give way?
A sailplane in free flight sees a powered aerotow converging from its left at the same level, away from a landing emergency. Which has priority?
options: The sailplane, while both must avoid collision
The aerotow has unconditional priority over the sailplane
The aircraft with the more powerful engine

questions.text: A powered aeroplane and a sailplane converge at approximately the same level. Which must give way?
options: Whichever is on the left, with no category exception

questions.text: In Class D, an IFR aeroplane in VMC converges with a VFR helicopter approaching from its right. Who normally gives way?
options: The aeroplane; IFR status alone does not give priority over the helicopter
The helicopter because VFR always yields to IFR
ATC clearance gives the aeroplane unconditional priority
The larger aircraft always has priority

questions.text: Two aeroplanes converge in VMC at the same level. Only one holds an ATC clearance. Does that clearance itself give right-of-way?
options: No; apply the normal right-of-way rules
Yes, if the aircraft is larger

questions.text: A powered aeroplane in free flight converges with another powered aircraft towing a glider. The tow is on its left. Who must give way?
options: The tow because it is on the left
The glider being towed must release

questions.text: A lower aeroplane has landing priority over a higher one. What may it still not do?
options: Cut in front of or overtake an aircraft already in final approach

questions.text: A non-commercial single-engine landplane flies over water beyond gliding distance of land. What individual flotation equipment is required under Part-NCO?
options: A readily accessible life-jacket for each person, with an equivalent device for a child under 24 months
Life rafts only, with no individual flotation
No flotation equipment if the flight is VFR
One life-jacket for the pilot only

questions.text: An airborne civil aircraft must comply with the general rules and which flight rules?
options: VFR whenever visibility is good, regardless of the flight plan

questions.text: What does an ATC clearance authorise?
options: Proceeding under the specified traffic conditions, while other applicable rules still apply
Guaranteed separation from every aircraft in all classes

questions.text: An ATC clearance would cause the pilot to breach an applicable rule. What should the pilot do?
options: Advise ATC and request an amended clearance
Accept it because ATC takes all legal responsibility
Accept it and report only after landing

questions.text: An emergency requires immediate deviation from the current ATC clearance. What follows as soon as practicable?
options: Notify the appropriate ATC unit of the action and seek any necessary amended clearance
Keep the deviation secret if it improves safety

questions.text: On being intercepted, what should a civil aircraft do unless the appropriate ATS unit instructs otherwise regarding the transponder?
options: Follow the interception signals, attempt contact on 121.5 MHz, and select 7700
Turn off the transponder and all lights

questions.text: An intercepting aircraft breaks away with an abrupt climbing turn of 90° or more without crossing your flight path. What does this signal mean?
An intercepting aircraft circles the aerodrome, lowers its landing gear and leads you toward the landing runway. What does Series 3 mean?
Two aeroplanes of the same category converge at approximately the same level. Which one must give way?
options: The aeroplane that has the other on its right
The aeroplane that has the other on its left

questions.text: Under SERA, what is the ordinary minimum height for day VFR outside congested areas, without a special permission or take-off/landing exception?
options: 500 ft above ground/water and 500 ft above obstacles within 150 m
1,000 ft above obstacles within 600 m everywhere
There is no minimum outside controlled airspace

questions.text: At night, another aeroplane stays on a constant relative bearing 050° at your level. You see its red navigation light. What should you conclude?
options: There is a collision risk and you must give way to the aircraft on your right
There is no risk because the bearing is constant
You have priority because you see red
The other aircraft must turn left

questions.text: A VFR-only pilot receives a heading instruction that would take the aircraft into cloud. What is the appropriate response?
options: Tell ATC immediately that the instruction cannot be followed while maintaining VMC and request an alternative
Enter cloud because ATC has taken responsibility

questions.text: Before entering a Class D control zone under a special VFR clearance, your radio fails. What is the appropriate action?
options: Remain outside the control zone and arrange a safe alternative
Enter because the original clearance overrides the radio requirement
Enter and rely only on light signals

questions.text: An ICAO certificate carries an endorsement that it does not fully meet an international standard. What is needed for international navigation into another State?
options: Permission from each State whose territory is entered
No permission if a flight plan is filed

questions.text: During descent through the transition level toward an aerodrome, which usual altimeter setting replaces standard pressure?
options: The cruise QNE expressed as hPa

questions.text: What is the transition level?
options: The lowest flight level available above the transition altitude
The transition altitude converted directly into a flight level

questions.text: At an uncontrolled aerodrome, which direction should an aeroplane normally use for take-off or landing if no safety, runway or traffic factor calls for another direction?
options: Across the wind in every case
Whichever direction the pilot first sees

questions.text: Under Part-FCL, for how long is successful PPL theoretical knowledge completion valid for licence issue?
Under Part-MED, what medical certificate normally permits exercise of PPL(A) privileges?
options: At least Class 2; a valid Class 1 also meets this requirement

questions.text: When must a student aeroplane pilot have a valid medical certificate before operating alone?
options: Only before the PPL skill test

questions.text: In the standard Part-FCL PPL(A) course, what is the maximum FSTD credit within the required 45 hours?
What is the standard Part-FCL PPL(A) qualifying solo cross-country requirement for one flight?
options: At least 150 NM with full-stop landings at two aerodromes other than departure

questions.text: In Part-FCL terminology, what is solo flight time?
options: Flight time when a student pilot is the sole occupant
All PIC time, including flights with passengers
Any time an instructor remains silent

questions.text: An instructor only observes a student acting as PIC, without influencing or controlling the flight. What is this defined time?
For SEP/TMG revalidation by experience, without an instructor-training exemption, which package must be completed in the 12 months preceding rating expiry?
options: 12 flight hours, including 6 PIC hours, 12 take-offs/landings and at least 1 hour refresher training with FI/CRI

questions.text: A pilot chooses proficiency-check revalidation of an SEP class rating. What is the normal window immediately before expiry?
Which convention established the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)?
options: The Convention on International Civil Aviation signed at Chicago

questions.text: Before starting a flight, what general information duty applies to the PIC?
options: Become familiar with all available information appropriate to the intended operation
Read only the aircraft maintenance log

questions.text: For a VFR flight away from the departure vicinity, what contingency must flight preparation include?
options: An alternative course of action if weather prevents completing the planned flight
A compulsory named IFR alternate for every local VFR flight
No alternative if the destination forecast is good

questions.text: When assessing a non-commercial aeroplane flight, how should the PIC establish that intended runways are usable?
options: Check runway lengths and the aircraft performance limitations/data for the conditions
Assume any licensed aerodrome accepts the aircraft
Rely on an ATC clearance as performance approval

questions.text: What must the PIC ensure passengers are told about safety belts before flight?
options: Nothing if passengers have flown before

questions.text: What is a prohibited area?
options: Defined airspace over a State’s land or territorial waters in which aircraft flight is prohibited
An area requiring only a flight plan
An area reserved exclusively for VFR

questions.text: A State reserves paid transport between two points in its own territory to its domestic operators. Which right does this illustrate?
options: The first freedom of the air
The second freedom of the air

questions.text: Under Part-FCL, can a CPL holder act as co-pilot in commercial air transport when the appropriate type rating and all other required qualifications are held?
options: Yes, subject to the applicable conditions
No; an ATPL is always required even for a co-pilot
Only if no passengers are carried

questions.text: Under Part-FCL, may a CPL holder act as PIC of a single-pilot aeroplane in commercial air transport if all relevant ratings and other conditions are met?
options: Yes, subject to the applicable CPL and recent-experience restrictions
No; every commercial flight requires an ATPL

questions.text: What does ditching describe in an aircraft emergency?
options: A deliberate emergency landing on water
A normal landing of a seaplane on water
An accidental collision with water during flight

questions.text: Under SERA, what should a VFR pilot normally do before entering a radio mandatory zone (RMZ)?
options: Make the required initial radio call, then maintain the prescribed radio watch and two-way communication as necessary
Select 7700 and enter without a call
Remain radio-silent unless ATC calls first
Treat the RMZ as automatically prohibited airspace

questions.text: Unless a published alternative applies, what SSR capability must an aircraft carry and operate in a transponder mandatory zone (TMZ)?
options: Modes A and C, or Mode S
Mode A only, with IDENT continuously selected
Any receiver capable of monitoring121.5 MHz
No transponder if the flight is VFR

questions.text: A VFR flight in Class C is cleared to FL100. The transition altitude is 5,000 ft AMSL. Under SERA, what minimum flight visibility normally applies?
Which cloud base defines the ceiling when several cloud layers are present?
options: The lowest qualifying cloud layer below 20,000 ft that covers more than half the sky, measured above ground or water
The highest cloud layer, measured above mean sea level
Any scattered layer regardless of coverage
The aircraft’s height above the highest cloud

questions.text: Under SERA, which code normally applies when an aircraft is not receiving air traffic services and the competent authority has prescribed no other code?
Under ordinary SERA rules, may a VFR aeroplane enter Class C airspace without an ATC clearance?
options: No; Class C requires an ATC clearance for VFR as well as IFR
Yes; only IFR flights need clearance in Class C
Yes, if the pilot uses the emergency transponder code
Yes; making a radio call always replaces a clearance

questions.text: For a non-commercial Part-NCO flight, fatigue prevents the PIC from safely performing flight duties. What is required before departure?
options: Do not commence the flight while incapacitated
Depart if the medical certificate is still in date
Depart if the flight will last less than one hour
Treat fatigue only as a passenger-comfort issue
